column3: The Hebrew repeats king before Shimron and Achshaph and does not explicitly name the things heard.
Close to the Hebrew.
The peoples have singular collective names in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “they” without repeating kings and uses collective singular horse and chariot.
The Hebrew separately says they came before camping.
The Hebrew says tomorrow about this time, rather than by this time, and explicitly mentions fire.
The Hebrew describes attacking them as falling on them.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says with fire.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not repeat the Israelites or Joshua as names here; it retains each soul and the mouth of the sword.
The Hebrew first names all the cities of these kings and then all their kings.
The Hebrew describes the cities as standing on their mounds.
The Hebrew retains the mouth of the sword.
The Hebrew says he did not turn aside anything of all that was commanded.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add western to the foothills.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew measures the period as many days.
The Hebrew gives the Hivite a singular collective name and actively says they took all in battle.
The heart is singular in the Hebrew, and the devoting and destroying are active infinitives rather than explicit passive clauses.
The Hebrew repeats from before Hebron, Debir, and Anab and repeats all the hill country before Israel.
Close to the Hebrew.
